web/composer/reasoning.py:R4:warn_if_not: R4 broad `except Exception` around `import litellm` + `litellm.supports_reasoning(model=model)` in `warn_if_not_reasoning_capable`. The function's entire product is one operator log line: its docstring states it never raises, and `apply_reasoning_kwargs` — the function that actually decides the call kwargs — is independent of it and runs whether or not the registry answers. The swallowed body contains NO ELSPETH-owned call: it is a third-party import plus one litellm registry lookup, so no audit-integrity or framework-invariant error can originate inside it and a `TIER_1_ERRORS` re-raise arm here would guard an unreachable path. What the swallow protects is boot: this runs at composer settings validation, and litellm's `supports_reasoning` registry is known-stale for the exact model strings ELSPETH ships (`openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` is False on litellm 1.85.0 while `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` is True — the reason `apply_reasoning_kwargs` carries the `openrouter/` carve-out at all), so an exception from a registry ELSPETH does not control must not deny service. The failure is NOT silent: the handler calls `_logger.warning` with `role`, `model` and `type(registry_failure).__name__`, naming the failure class while deliberately withholding the exception text, which for a provider-registry lookup can carry gateway URLs, credentials-adjacent config or filesystem paths. Value tier is not the issue at this site — `model` and `role` are Tier-1 settings-derived strings validated by `apply_reasoning_kwargs`, which RAISES `ValueError` on an unknown effort; the broad catch covers only the advisory lookup, not any parse.
web/composer/discovery_cache.py:R5:pydan: R5 `isinstance(obj, BaseModel)` in `pydantic_default`, the `default=` hook `serialize_tool_result` hands to `json.dumps`. `type(obj) is BaseModel` is not a candidate substitution and would be a defect: `BaseModel` is never instantiated directly, every value that legitimately reaches this hook is a pydantic SUBCLASS instance, and an exact-type test would reject all of them and raise `TypeError` on every real model. Subclassing IS pydantic's declared extension contract, which is what makes this nominal typing rather than structural: ADR-032 forbids a `runtime_checkable` Protocol as a dispatch control precisely because an impostor duck-types past it, and `isinstance` against a concrete declared base class is the mechanism the ADR prescribes instead. The value is Tier-1/2 server data, not parsed external input — `obj` is reached only from `ToolResult.to_dict()`, a server-constructed composer tool envelope — so `@trust_boundary` here would be a false external-source claim. What the check protects is the serializer's honesty: the negative arm raises `TypeError` naming `type(obj).__name__` rather than emitting a lossy or fabricated JSON value for an object ELSPETH cannot canonically serialize, so an unserializable field surfaces as a hard failure at the cache/serialize seam instead of reaching a session payload as silently degraded data.
web/composer/advisor_checkpoint_telemetr: R7 `with suppress(Exception)` around the `slog.info("composer.advisor_checkpoint_pass", ...)` emit in `record_advisor_checkpoint_pass`. The suppressed call IS the recording channel, so there is by construction no lower channel that could record its own failure — logging is the recovery path of last resort under the audit > telemetry > logger primacy that `elspeth.engine._best_effort.best_effort` documents, and a structlog processor or sink outage cannot be reported to structlog. The control that makes the swallow safe is therefore upstream, not downstream: the caller's checkpoint verdict is already complete and returned before this helper is entered — this function's own docstring and its `AdvisorCheckpointTelemetryVerdict` parameter carry a verdict that has already been decided — so nothing about the advisor decision is lost when the event is dropped. An ELSPETH invariant error cannot be swallowed here: `stable_hash` (elspeth.contracts.hashing) is the only owned call in the emit and it is now computed ABOVE the `suppress` into `findings_hash`, so its `ValueError` on a non-finite float and its `TypeError` on a frozenset propagate as the programmer errors they are. This is the same guard ordering the signed `web/composer/telemetry_phase8.py` per-file R4 exemption relies on (its `_assert_session_trust_mode` / `_assert_completion_verb` guards fire before the try). What remains inside the suppression is exclusively third-party structlog dispatch. Bounding note: the event carries `findings_hash`, never `findings_text` — raw advisor findings must not be recursively logged.

R7 `with suppress(Exception)` around `_ADVISOR_CHECKPOINT_PASSES_COUNTER.add(1, {"phase": phase, "verdict": verdict})` in `record_advisor_checkpoint_pass`. The suppressed body is a single OpenTelemetry counter increment: no ELSPETH-owned call is inside it, so no audit-integrity or framework-invariant error can originate there and there is nothing for a `TIER_1_ERRORS` arm to catch. `suppress` rather than `try/except Exception: return None` is the deliberate shape because this is the LAST statement of the helper and the two emits are intentionally independent — a failed event sink must not skip the metric and a failed exporter must not skip the event — which is why the two suppressions are siblings rather than one block. The control that makes the swallow safe is the caller's already-decided checkpoint verdict, complete before this helper runs (the `verdict` argument is that decision, not a value computed here); the counter is operational accounting for how many checkpoint passes ran, never the record of what a pass concluded. Both attributes are Tier-1 closed literals — `phase` is `AdvisorCheckpointPhase` and `verdict` is `AdvisorCheckpointTelemetryVerdict`, both `Literal` unions — so a malformed attribute cannot originate at this site either. Same adjudicated shape and rationale as the signed `web/composer/telemetry_phase8.py` per-file R4 exemption: a broken OTel exporter must not fail a composer request whose decision has already been made.
web/composer/tutorial_telemetry.py:R4:re: R4 broad `except Exception` around `_TUTORIAL_COMPLETED_COUNTER.add(1, attributes={"completion_path": completion_path})` in `record_tutorial_completed_path`. This is the same mechanism, in the same package, as the operator-signed per-file R4 exemption for `web/composer/telemetry_phase8.py` (`try: <counter>.add(...) / except Exception: return None`), and it is justified on the identical ground: the outcome this counter describes has ALREADY committed. The helper is called after the tutorial-completion preference write persists, so a broken OTel exporter raising here would fail a request whose durable state was already written — inverting audit-over-telemetry primacy by making a secondary channel able to invalidate a completed primary one. The programmer-error guard is preserved in the shape the signed entry requires: the `completion_path not in _COMPLETION_PATHS` check raises `ValueError` BEFORE the `try`, so an unknown path is a loud crash and only exporter failure is swallowed — pinned by `tests/unit/web/composer/test_tutorial_telemetry.py::test_record_tutorial_completed_rejects_unknown_path`. No ELSPETH-owned call is inside the handler's protected body, so no `TIER_1_ERRORS` can be swallowed; `completion_path` is a Tier-1 server-derived `_CompletionPath` literal, never a client-supplied string. Swallow behaviour is pinned by `test_completed_telemetry_does_not_replace_committed_outcome`, which drives a `_FailingCounter` and asserts the helper still returns `None`. ADR-031 note: this is a metric counter, not an authoring path — it adds no tutorial-only branch to any composer code path.

R4 broad `except Exception` around `_TUTORIAL_ABANDON_COUNTER.add(1, attributes={})` in `record_tutorial_abandoned`, the same adjudicated telemetry-only shape as the signed `web/composer/telemetry_phase8.py` per-file R4 exemption. This one is a page-unload beacon: `create_tutorial_abandon_router` returns 204 and the browser has already navigated away, so there is no client left to receive an error and nothing downstream that a raise could usefully inform — an unavailable exporter would convert a best-effort beacon into a 500 in the server's own logs for a request whose user is gone. The counter is pure operational accounting for how many first-run tutorials were abandoned; it carries no audit meaning and no state depends on it. The protected body is one OpenTelemetry counter increment with an empty attributes mapping — no ELSPETH-owned call, hence no `TIER_1_ERRORS` reachable to swallow, and no Tier-3 value read anywhere in the function (it takes no arguments). Both the 204 route contract and the swallow are pinned: `tests/unit/web/composer/test_tutorial_telemetry.py::test_abandon_route_increments_counter` asserts the increment on the happy path and `::test_abandon_telemetry_is_best_effort` drives a `_FailingCounter` and asserts the helper still returns `None`. ADR-031 note: a counter increment, not an authoring path — no tutorial-only branch is introduced into any composer code path.
